City Council Meeting
Public Comment from the Audience
•
If you wish to address the City Council, please complete a Speaker Request Card, as it must be handed to the City Clerk before the start of the meeting.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on matters not listed on the agenda during the Public Comments from the Audience period.
•
Opportunity to address the City Council (on non-agenda items) is limited to 3 minutes per speaker.
•
The City Council will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote.
Brown Act
Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.
Rules of Decorum
Persons attending the meeting shall observe rules of propriety, decorum, good conduct, and refrain from impertinent or slanderous remarks. Violation of this rule shall result in such persons being barred from further audience before the governing body. Pursuant to Gov. Code Sect. 54954.3(c), any person who engages in unlawful interference shall be removed from chambers.
Americans with Disabilities Act
In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, please contact the City Clerk's office at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to allow the City to make reasonable arrangements to ensure accessibility to the meeting or service.
This agenda was posted 72 hours in advance of the meeting at the City Hall, 8838 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; the L.A. County Library, Rosemead Branch, 8800 E. Valley Boulevard, Rosemead; and other locations pursuant to RMC Sec. 1.08.020. Any writings or documents provided to a majority of the Rosemead City Council regarding any item on this agenda will be made available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours.

MATTERS FROM CITY COUNCIL
A.
Active Duty Military Leave for Council Member Ly; and Consideration of Temporary Appointment of Jean Hall to the City Council
Council Member Steven Ly has been ordered by the United States Army Reserve to report to active duty for training effective on July 13, 2015, for a period of 144 days. Prior to reporting for active military duty, Council Member Ly recommended that the City Council appoint Traffic Commissioner Jean Hall to serve in his place on the City Council during his absence. In response, Ms. Hall has expressed a willingness to serve in this temporary capacity. The City Council will consider the appointment of Jean Hall to serve on the City Council on a temporary basis until Council Member Steven Ly returns from active military duty in December.
Recommendation: That the City Council appoint Jean Hall to serve on the City Council during Council Member Lyâ€™s absence due to active military service in the United States Army Reserve.

B.
Ordinance No. 951 â€“ Second Reading: Approving Municipal Code Amendment (MCA) 15-02 and Amending Chapters 17.04 and 17.72 of Title 17 of the City of Rosemead Municipal Code Relating to Regulations for Nonconforming Uses, Structures, Lots, and Parking Facilities.
On June 9, 2015, the City Council introduced Ordinance No. 951, approving MCA 15-02 and amending Chapters 17.04 and 17.72 of Title 17 of the City of Rosemead Municipal Code relating to regulations for Nonconforming Uses, Structures, Lots, and Parking Facilities. Ordinance No. 951 is now before Council at the required second reading for adoption.
Recommendation: That the City Council Adopt Ordinance No. 951 at its second reading.
C.
Adoption of Resolution 2015-42 Setting the Fee for Shopping Cart Containment Plan
On February 24, 2015 the City Council adopted Ordinance No. 937 adding section 9.32 to the Cityâ€™s Municipal Code relating to shopping cart retrieval and containment by owners. Section 9.32.060 states that â€œeach proposed plan shall be accompanied by a processing fee in an amount as set by resolution of the City Council. No proposed plan shall be accepted for filing and processing by the Planning Division unless accompanied by the processing fee established by the City Council.â€ Since this entire process was new and City staff was unsure of the time involved to review the plans, a fee was not immediately established. Now that the Planning Division has been working with businesses to receive and review shopping cart retrieval and containment plans, itâ€™s been determined that these plans require a significant amount of staff time and cost recovery in full is likely not feasible. Full cost recovery for the review and approval of these plans would be in excess of $500. In order to be business friendly while enforcing these regulations, staff is proposing a fee of $100.
Recommendation: That the City Council adopt Resolution 2015-42 authorizing the Shopping Cart Retrieval and Containment Plan fee.
D.
Approval of Professional Services Agreements for on-call Engineering Services
The City utilizes professional consultant services for the design of major capital projects involving street, landscaping, transportation, and utility improvements. As the work load requires, staff will utilize these firms to perform design services, traffic engineering studies, public works inspection services, review of private development projects, geotechnical services, survey work, and special analyses. The attached on-call professional services agreements will continue to provide the City with the ability to obtain multiple bids for services on a project by project basis and help ensure efficient service delivery to the community.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve the professional services agreements with the attached engineering services firms to provide as needed on-call professional services and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreements.
E.
Authorized Signers on Bank Accounts â€“ City Council Resolution No. 2015-43 and Successor Agency Resolution No. 2015-15
The City of Rosemead (City) and the Successor Agency for the Rosemead Community Development Commission (Successor Agency) require several different bank accounts to efficiently operate financial matters. Authorized signers on both the Cityâ€™s and the Successor Agencyâ€™s accounts include all City Council members, the Mayor, the Mayor Pro Tem, the City Manager, the Assistant City Manager and the City Clerk.
Recommendation: That the City Council approve Resolution No. 2015-43 and Successor Agency Resolution No. 2015-15 authorizing the Mayor, Mayor Pro Tem, City Council members, City Manager and Assistant City Manager as signers on the Cityâ€™s bank accounts at Bank of the West.
F.
Authorized Signers on Bank Accounts â€“ RHDC Resolution No. 2015-08
The Rosemead Housing Development Corporation (RHDC) requires a checking account to efficiently operate its financial matters. Authorized signers on the RHDCâ€™s account include all RHDC Directors, the President, the Vice President, the Executive Director and the Assistant City Manager.
Recommendation: That the RHDC Board approve Resolution No. 2015-08 authorizing the President, Vice President, Directors, Executive Director and Assistant City Manager as signers on the RHDC bank account; remove the name of the former Secretary, Gloria Molleda; and appoint the Interim City Clerk, Carol Cowley as the Corporation Secretary until a replacement Secretary can be appointed.
G.
Confirmation of Appointment of Interim City Clerk
The City Council will consider confirmation of the appointment of Interim City Clerk Carol Cowley. The City Clerk position became vacant on July 2, 2015. As the result of a competitive selection process, the City Manager appointed Carol Cowley as Interim City Clerk on a temporary basis effective on July 7, 2015. Upon confirmation of this appointment, it is envisioned that Ms. Cowley will be employed as Interim City Clerk through December of 2015 until a new City Clerk is appointed by the City Council.
Recommendation: That the City Council confirm the temporary appointment of Carol Cowley as Interim City Clerk

MATTERS FROM CITY MANAGER & STAFF
A.
Paratransit System Update
As the City Council is aware, the contract for paratransit services in the City of Rosemead (Dial-a-Ride and Fixed Route) expired on June 30, 2015. Southland Transit is continuing operation of the paratransit services on a month-to-month contract until the Request for Proposals (RFP) process is completed and a new contract is issued. The City Council will be presented with staffâ€™s recommendation for services at the August 11, 2015 meeting and service under the new contract is expected to begin October 1, 2015. Part of this new service includes the elimination of commuter connect services between the Rosemead Place shopping center and the El Monte transit depot and Metrolink station due to high costs and low ridership numbers.
Recommendation: That the City Council provide input and direction regarding the transit system RFP or bus acquisition process if any changes are required.
